title: Show per-turn file changes summary for agent host chat responses
body:
Fix #318891

## What

Renders the collapsible **"Changed N files"** summary under completed **agent host** chat responses when `chat.checkpoints.showFileChanges` is enabled. Until now this summary only appeared for regular local chat sessions; agent host responses skipped it.

The summary is driven by the **per-turn changeset** the agent host computes server-side — the same authoritative source backing the Agents window Changes view — rather than the chat editing session. This means it reflects all of a turn's changes (including edits made via terminal/external tools), not just the ones tracked through chat's own edit pipeline.

## How

- **`IChatResponseFileChangesService`** (new): a small per-session-type provider registry. `ChatCheckpointFileChangesSummaryContentPart` consults it first and falls back to the chat editing session for non-agent-host sessions, so local chat is unchanged. The summary part now **self-hides** when its resolved diffs are empty, so a turn that made no edits shows nothing.
- **`AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider`** (new): for a given response it subscribes to the session's per-turn changeset (keyed by the response's turn id), gated on the agent advertising a `turn` changeset, and maps the changeset files into edit-session diffs. Subscriptions are lazy and memoized per request.
- **Renderer gate**: `getChatFileChangesSummaryPart` now creates the summary part for agent host responses (which emit external edits rather than text/notebook edit groups); the existing gate is unchanged for other sessions.
- **Shared `normalizeFileEdit` helper**: extracts the create/delete/rename/edit detection and URI parsing that was duplicated across the external-edit, snapshot, and changeset mappers.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the `normalizeFileEdit` helper (all four file statuses) and the agent host provider (mapping, empty-when-no-turn-changeset, memoization).
- Existing snapshot-controller, state-adapter, and sessions-provider suites still pass after the refactor.
- Manual smoke test against a real Copilot agent host session: the summary renders with correct file list and +/- counts; the modified-file diff resolves before-content correctly in the editor window; a no-edit turn shows no summary.

### Known v1 caveat

For **created** files there is no before-content, so opening that file's diff shows no delta (the summary's +/- counts are still correct since they come from the server). The same class of edge case applies to deletions.

(Written by Copilot)

title: agentHost: implement Claude truncateSession (Phase 6.7 — Restore Checkpoint + Start Over)
body:
## What

Implements `IAgent.truncateSession` for the Claude agent host, so the workbench's **Restore Checkpoint** and **Start Over** actions work end-to-end for Claude sessions (previously a no-op — only Copilot supported it).

This is **Phase 6.7** of the Claude agent-host roadmap. Full implementation log: `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/phase6.7-plan.md`; roadmap entry marked done in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/roadmap.md`.

## How

Two flows, both keeping the **same** SDK session id / protocol URI (unlike fork, which mints a new id):

- **Restore Checkpoint (point-restore, `turnId`)** — truncates the conversation in place via the SDK's `resumeSessionAt` option. The protocol turn is resolved to its SDK assistant-envelope uuid (reusing Phase 6.5's `resolveForkAnchorUuid`) and staged as a one-shot anchor the next turn's rebuild applies. The write is **lazy**: if the user restores then walks away without sending, the full pre-restore history is preserved.
- **Start Over (remove-all, no `turnId`)** — tears down the live subprocess, deletes the on-disk transcript, and recreates a fresh provisional under the same id, preserving the model/agent/permissionMode overlay.

### Notable sub-fixes
- **Deterministic teardown** — remove-all awaits the subprocess's actual exit (`Query.return()` → the SDK's memoized `cleanup()` → `transport.waitForExit()`) before deleting + respawning the same `--session-id`. Without this, the dying process re-flushed `<id>.jsonl` and the respawn failed with `Session ID … is already in use`.
- **Rebind consumer-loop handoff** — fixed a pre-existing race (surfaced by truncation) where a post-restore turn could hang because the consumer loop didn't hand off to the rebound query.
- **Pipeline handle simplification** — collapsed three overlapping query/process handles to two with one clear meaning each: `_warm` (subprocess), `_query` (the stream bound to it, lifetime mirrors `_warm`), and `_needsRebind` as the sole health signal.

## Testing

- **Unit/integration:** 427 Claude tests pass (incl. new coverage for `resumeSessionAt` projection, warm + cold point-restore, warm + cold remove-all, teardown ordering, the rebind handoff, and the post-abort steering guard).
- **Gates:** typecheck-client, valid-layers-check, eslint, hygiene all clean.
- **Live E2E (real Claude):** both flows verified — Restore Checkpoint (BANANA/ELEPHANT memory test: model forgot the truncated turn) and Start Over (clean recreate on same id), each across two cycles with zero `already in use` / `stream ended` / `exit-1` / `crashed` errors across an 8-turn session.

title: Show only cloud coding agent tasks in cloud sessions list (v2)
body:
## Problem

With the Task API (v2) cloud agent backend, the cloud sessions list shows entries that don't belong there:

1. **Local sessions leak in.** The v2 `fetchSessionList` listed *all* non-archived Mission Control tasks. Local VS Code / Copilot CLI / JetBrains sessions are mirrored into Mission Control as tasks, so they showed up alongside genuine cloud coding-agent sessions (the VS Code–icon rows in the agents list).
2. **Settled tasks stuck on "In Progress".** Cloud tasks settle into `idle` / `waiting_for_user` (not `completed`). The legacy `SessionInfo['state']` shape collapses both into `in_progress`, so the status badge was stuck on InProgress.

## Fix

**Cloud-only filter.** A task's owning surface is identified by the agent integration slug on its `agent_collaborators`:

| Slug | Surface | Shown? |
|---|---|---|
| `copilot-developer` (CMC/CAPI) / `copilot-swe-agent` (monolith) | Cloud coding agent | ✅ |
| `copilot-developer-cli` | Copilot CLI | ❌ |
| `vscode-chat` | Copilot in VS Code | ❌ |
| `jetbrains-chat` | Copilot in JetBrains | ❌ |

Adds an exported pure helper `isCloudCodingAgentTask(task)` (whitelist of cloud slugs) and applies it in `fetchSessionList`. This mirrors GitHub's own first-party clients, which filter the same list client-side by reading `agent_collaborators[].slug` (see github-ui `agent-helpers.ts` / `agent-profile.ts`). `agent_collaborators` is returned to first-party CAPI tokens but isn't modeled yet in `@vscode/copilot-api`, so a minimal local type is used at the call site.

**Status mapping.** Carries the raw `AgentTaskState` across the backend seam (`CloudSessionData.taskState`) and maps it directly to `ChatSessionStatus` in the provider (`taskStateToChatSessionStatus`), so `idle` → Completed and `waiting_for_user` → NeedsInput instead of collapsing to InProgress. The lossy v1 `SessionInfo['state']` is left untouched (it can't express NeedsInput).

## Notes / tradeoffs

- The cloud filter is a **whitelist**: a genuinely-cloud task only appears once CMC has populated its `agent_collaborators` with a recognized cloud slug. Custom / third-party cloud agents with other slugs won't show — easy to broaden later by adding slugs to the set.
- No change to `mapTaskStateToSessionState` (v1 shape) or to the v1 `JobsApiBackend`.

## Validation

- `tsgo --noEmit`: clean for touched files.
- `vitest` spec `copilotCloudSessionsProvider.spec.ts`: 23 passing, including new coverage for the cloud-only filter, `isCloudCodingAgentTask`, and the `taskState` → `ChatSessionStatus` mapping.
- `eslint --max-warnings=0`: clean.

title: Expose reveal scroll-alignment to the TreeView API (and an Explorer/SCM "reveal with context" option)
body:
## Feature request

When a tree item is revealed — either programmatically via the extension `TreeView.reveal()` API, or by built-in auto-reveal in the Explorer / Source Control views — the item is scrolled to the **top edge** of the viewport, with no surrounding rows visible. You lose all sense of *where* the item sits among its siblings (the files immediately above/below it).

The underlying list/tree widget already supports revealing an element at a **fractional vertical position** internally (the tree's `reveal(element, relativeTop)` / list `reveal` plumbing). That capability just isn't surfaced anywhere a consumer can reach it:

1. **Extension API gap** — `TreeView.reveal(element, { select, focus, expand })` has no option to control scroll alignment. An extension that reveals a node cannot ask for it to be centered or shown with surrounding context; it always lands pinned to the top.
2. **No user setting** — Explorer / SCM auto-reveal always pins the revealed item to the top edge. `explorer.autoReveal` is only `true | false | "focusNoScroll"`, and `focusNoScroll` *suppresses* scrolling, which is the opposite of wanting context.

## Proposal

1. Add an optional alignment to the `TreeView.reveal` options, e.g. `reveal(element, { select, focus, expand, alignment?: 'top' | 'center' })` (or a numeric `relativeTop`), surfacing the existing internal capability to extensions.
2. Optionally, a user setting for built-in auto-reveal alignment, e.g. `explorer.revealAlignment` / `scm.revealAlignment`: `"top" | "center"`.

## Why this isn't a duplicate

Earlier discussions (#63406, and related #23902 / #65549) led to *removing* always-centered reveal in favour of top-pinning. This request isn't asking to flip the default back — it asks to make alignment **configurable / API-exposed** so both preferences are served, rather than hard-coding one. The "reveal with context" behaviour matters for review workflows where an extension steps through items and reveals each one.

## Use case

I maintain a git-diff-review extension that reveals the file currently under review in the SCM/Explorer tree as the user steps through changes. Because reveal pins to the top edge, the reviewed file ends up flush against the top with no visible context. An alignment option (or a `relativeTop`) would let the extension reveal it with a few rows of breathing room above and below.

body: ## What In an untrusted (**Restricted Mode**) workspace, the Agent Host model picker (Copilot CLI / Claude) loaded models and showed **"Auto"**, instead of the **"Pick Model" + Trust Workspace** affordance that the Local harness correctly shows. Specifically addresses https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322564#issuecomment-4811816607. ## Why The agent-host harnesses (`claude-code`, `copilotcli`) register their session-scoped models **without a workspace-trust gate** (`claudeCodeModels.ts`, `copilotCli.ts`), so those models stay live in Restricted Mode. `getModelPickerUnavailableReason` treated any live, picker-offered model as usable and returned "available", masking the Restricted state. General-purpose models are withheld while untrusted, which is why the Local harness behaved correctly. ## Fix `getModelPickerUnavailableReason` now reports `Restricted` for an untrusted workspace **before** the "a live picker-offered model wins" check. A single change fixes every picker that routes through this function (chat editor input + sessions config bar). ## Feature request

Please add support for VS Code Copilot agents to read PDF files.

## Problem

Many engineering and scientific projects depend on vendor manuals, datasheets, and safety documents that are distributed as PDFs. Currently, users must extract the text from PDFs and save it to a `.txt` or `.md` file, but plain text extraction loses important information.

- Tables are flattened, reordered, or lose headers
- Images, figures, wiring diagrams, and plots are completely lost
- Captions may be separated from the associated figure
- Page numbers and section references can be lost
- Extracted text lose structure and may create incorrect context for the agent

It's difficult to trust that Copilot agents have the correct context when they can only read copy-and-paste text from the user manual.

## Desired behavior

When a PDF is present in a VS Code workspace, Copilot agents should be able correctly read and understand it.

PDF support should handle both scanned/image-based PDFs and vector/text-based PDFs.

title: build(oss): retry CG notice generation and widen platform poll budget
body:
🤖 AI Assisted PR

Two small hardening changes to the CG-based ThirdPartyNotices pipeline:

1. **Retry CG generation** — add `retryCountOnTaskFailure: 3` to the `notice@0` step in `product-quality-checks.yml`. A transient hard failure now retries in place before degrading to the cached-NOTICE fallback. CG succeeds in ~15–30s, so retries add negligible wall-clock and only fire on a non-zero exit. (Soft "exit 0 but empty output" failures are still caught by the existing >1KB check, not by this retry.)

2. **Widen platform poll budget** — bump `POLL_ATTEMPTS` 20 → 30 in `downloadNotice.ts` (10 → 15 min). Green builds accept the NOTICE artifact by attempt ~10, but during a real CG outage a slow Quality stage pushed platform polling to ~19–20, and one platform exhausted the budget and shipped the legacy notice while its peers shipped the CG notice (build 450982). The extra headroom prevents that cross-arch mismatch. No cost on healthy builds — they still exit early.

title: chat: fix stranded "input needed" agent-host session on client-tool reconnect
body:
## Problem

A paused agent-host chat session shows **"input needed"** but renders no confirmation/question — the session is stuck and the agent waits forever. From the incident logs:

- Session status is `SessionStatus.InputNeeded` (24).
- The active turn is blocked on a **client** tool (`problems` / `copilot_getErrors`).
- During reconnect, `Tool called for unknown chat session` is thrown and **no `ChatToolCallComplete` is ever dispatched back**, so the backend turn never unblocks.

## Root cause

When `provideChatSessionContent` reconnects to an existing session whose active turn is blocked on a client tool, it called `_reconnectToActiveTurn` **synchronously, before the chat model for that session was registered in `IChatService`**. Reconnect re-invokes the blocked client tool, and `LanguageModelToolsService.invokeTool` looks the model up by session resource and throws `Tool called for unknown chat session` when it is not yet present. The throw happens *before* any completion is dispatched, so the backend stays blocked indefinitely.

This is an ordering race: it only bites turns blocked on a **client** tool at the moment of reconnect (server-tool turns and freshly-created sessions are unaffected, which is why it was easy to miss).

## Fix

1. **Defer reconnect until the model exists (the actual fix).** Gate `_reconnectToActiveTurn` on `IChatService.getSession(...)`; if the model isn't registered yet, wait for `onDidCreateModel` for this session resource before reconnecting. This mirrors the **existing** snapshot-controller guard a few lines above (`getSession` / `onDidCreateModel`), so the two reconnect-time hooks now order the same way.

2. **Don't strand the turn on a pre-execution tool failure (defense in depth).** In `_setupClientToolCall`'s `handleSettled`, a non-cancellation pre-execution failure previously only logged a warning and returned, dispatching nothing. It now dispatches a failed `ChatToolCallComplete` (`success: false`) so any future pre-execution rejection surfaces as a tool result instead of an indefinite hang. The cancellation path is unchanged (still handled by the confirmation autorun dispatching `ChatToolCallConfirmed approved:false`).

## Tests

Adds two repro tests to `agentHostClientTools.test.ts`:

- `defers client tool invocation on reconnect until the chat model is registered`
- `reports a pre-execution client tool failure so the turn is not stranded`

Both **fail without** the handler change and **pass with** it; the 16 existing tests stay green (18 total). The test harness was made faithful to the real `LanguageModelToolsService` / `IChatService.getSession` behavior (default presents a model synchronously; `deferModel` opts into the realistic "model created after content" flow that triggers the race).

## Reviewer note

The two changes are intentionally layered: change **#1 removes the race** that produced this specific incident; change **#2 is a safety net** so *any* pre-execution client-tool failure can't silently strand a turn. I'd appreciate scrutiny on whether #1 is the true root cause vs. whether #2 is masking a deeper invariant (e.g. should reconnect ever be attempted before the model exists at all?).

(Written by Copilot)

title: Support subagent costs for local agent
Agent auto-persists referenceable/feature-specific knowledge into always-loaded global memory, inflating per-turn context cost

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.x (current, June 2026)
- VS Code Version: 1.127.x
- OS Version: Windows 11
- Feature: agent mode — memory tool (auto-write behavior)
- Selected model: Claude (Opus/Sonnet class)
- Logs: see measured evidence below

### Shared context (this issue has a sibling: #323167)
Both this issue and #323167 stem from the memory feature operating silently/automatically. The auto-write behavior described here continually grows /memories/ files, and the corruption bug in #323167 then multiplies that content — so the two compound each other (silent context bloat + data corruption).

### Core defect
In agent mode the model auto-persists **feature-specific and already-referenceable knowledge** into **always-loaded global memory** (`/memories/`). The first ~200 lines of user/global memory are injected into context on **every turn, in every workspace**, indefinitely. This is the wrong storage tier for this kind of content, for three reasons:

1. **Duplication of referenceable knowledge.** Feature details that already live in retrievable `docs/` files (or repo memory) get copied into always-loaded memory. The same information that a one-time on-demand `read_file` could supply *only when relevant* is instead injected into context on every turn forever. Same data, loaded continuously instead of on access — negative value.

2. **No relevance scoping.** Global memory loads in every workspace regardless of topic. A partner servicing N customers ends up loading, in customer X's sessions, customer Y's feature notes. Even within a single app, knowledge for feature A is loaded while working on unrelated feature B.

3. **Unbounded time cost.** A feature you don't touch for 3–4 years is still loaded on every turn in the interim, with zero corresponding use, and nothing ages it out.

### The principle being violated
Always-loaded persistent memory should hold only **small, cross-cutting, non-referenceable** facts (durable preferences, hard-won gotchas). Anything that is **(a) already retrievable from a doc, or (b) feature/workspace-specific** should NOT be auto-written to global memory — it should stay in `docs/` (or at most repo-scoped, on-demand memory) and be pulled only when relevant. The current `<memoryInstructions>` ("record what you learned") pushes the agent to do the opposite.

### Reproduced cross-workspace leak (captured this session)
I have a multi-root setup with separate workspaces. One workspace contains **only** a Business Central (AL) app and has **no knowledge of, and no files from, a separate React Native mobile app**. From that BC-only workspace I asked the agent — explicitly forbidding it from searching or reading any files — what it knew about the mobile app's PO-extraction work.

It answered with mobile/Python-pipeline feature specifics (`operating_pressure_psi` as a per-`part_item` schema field, the Phase A/B/C structure, a "mobile applier" that reads `shipping_resolved.agent_code/service_code` and falls back to `carrierHint`/`serviceLevelHint` on `csr_confirm`) and **explicitly attributed all of it to an auto-loaded global memory note**, `PO-Extract-Phase2-Handoff.md`. Verbatim from its reply:

> "Where the knowledge came from: Entirely from my persistent user-memory file … specifically the auto-loaded note `PO-Extraction-Phase2-Handoff.md` (under user memory). Nothing here came from reading the workspace, `app/docs/`, or any `.ts`/`.tsx` file in this session."

Notably it also correctly declined to fabricate the parts the note didn't contain — so the attribution is credible, not a hallucination. This is a concrete demonstration that feature-specific notes from one workspace are loaded into an unrelated workspace's context, with zero relevance to the task at hand.

### Measured evidence (real machine, single user)
- User/global memory: 26,438 bytes ≈ 6,610 tokens, auto-loaded every turn, every workspace
- Much of it is feature-specific content that already exists in this repo's `docs/` (e.g. PO-extraction internals) — i.e. duplicated, not unique
- All memory across all workspaces: 24 files, 156,069 bytes ≈ 39,017 tokens
- Example of mis-tiered content: workspace-specific feature notes (`phys-inv-*`, `PO-Extract-*`) auto-written to globally-loaded memory rather than left in retrievable docs

### Cost / impact (corrected — important)
The primary cost on a **GitHub Copilot subscription is NOT direct dollars.** Copilot meters by **premium request, not tokens** — one prompt in agent mode = one premium request × the model's multiplier, with tool calls and autonomous steps excluded, and overage billed per request ($0.04/request). Token volume inside a request does not change the billed amount. So on Copilot the real cost of this bloat is:

- **Context-window dilution and answer-quality degradation** — every turn spends a fixed slice of the window on irrelevant, often duplicated, cross-workspace notes.
- **Compounding with #323167** — corrupted/duplicated memory enlarges that always-loaded slice further.

The dollar cost only materializes under **per-token billing (Anthropic API / BYOK)**. As an order-of-magnitude reference there: ~6,610 tokens × ~420 sessions/month ≈ ~2.8M input tokens/month; at an Opus-class list rate of roughly $15 / 1M input tokens that is on the order of ~$40/month — but this does NOT apply to a standard Copilot subscription, where the same usage is $0 at the margin.

### Requests
1. **Stop auto-persisting referenceable/feature-specific content to always-loaded memory.** Prefer leaving it in `docs/` (or on-demand repo memory) and reading it only when relevant. Reserve global memory for small, cross-cutting facts.
2. **Relevance-scope what is loaded** — don't inject every workspace's notes into every other workspace's context.
3. **Age out / cap** stale entries, and surface the memory store's size and context footprint in the UI.
4. Allow `copilot-instructions.md` / project config to suppress or constrain memory writes (ref #308669).
5. (Secondary) make global memory writes opt-in or per-write confirmable.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Use agent mode normally over several sessions with the memory tool available, in a multi-root / multi-workspace setup.
2. Observe that feature-specific notes — content that already exists in retrievable `docs/` — are auto-written to `/memories/` without an explicit request to "save this."
3. From an unrelated workspace, ask the agent (forbidding file reads) about a feature that only exists in another workspace; it will recite it from auto-loaded global memory and attribute it to that note.

### Related
- #323167 — memory file corruption (recursive self-duplication) that enlarges this always-loaded slice
- #308669 — `<memoryInstructions>` cannot be overridden by copilot-instructions.md

body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.x (current, June 2026)
- VS Code Version: 1.127.x

- Selected model: Claude Opus 4.8

### Shared context (this issue has a sibling)
Both this issue and a companion issue stem from the memory feature operating silently/automatically. The auto-write behavior continually grows /memories/ files, and this corruption bug then multiplies that content — so the two compound each other (silent data loss + recurring token cost on every read).

### Summary
The memory tool can corrupt a memory file by recursively re-injecting the entire file body into itself. A series of `str_replace` / `insert` edits on a single `/memories/repo/` file caused the file's H1 header block and intro paragraph to be duplicated ~15 times, nested inside unrelated later sections, growing the file from ~3 KB to ~42 KB. The duplicated content is not a clean append — it is interleaved into the middle of existing sections, so the file is no longer coherent.

### Measured evidence (one real corrupted file)
- File: `repo/phys-inv-terminology.md`
- Size: 42,185 bytes / 720 lines (should be ~3 KB / ~60 lines)
- The H1 `# Physical Inventory — terminology (DO NOT re-derive)` appears 15 times (should be 1)
- The "one physical shelf" intro block appears 15 times, recursively nested inside unrelated later sections
- ~10,546 tokens per read; unique payload ≈ 700 tokens → ~93% duplicated garbage
- The corrupted file is auto-loaded / read back on subsequent turns, so the bloat is paid repeatedly

### Relationship to #322625
#322625 ("Memory str_replace tool silently drops large newString values") notes our exact symptom as a related observation — "mid-file content duplication (a header block was injected into an unrelated section)." This issue is a concrete, quantified instance with a reproducible artifact. The two may share a root cause at the JSON-RPC serialization boundary for large `newString` values (~4–6 KB+).

### Impact
- Silent data corruption of user memory files
- Recurring token cost: every read of the corrupted file pays ~10.5K tokens for ~700 tokens of real content
- The user cannot easily tell a file is corrupted without manually inspecting byte size / line count

### Steps to reproduce
1. Have a `/memories/repo/` (or `/memories/`) file longer than ~150–200 lines.
2. Issue several `str_replace` and/or `insert` edits whose `newString` is a multi-line block containing backticks / tables / fenced code, roughly 4–6 KB each.
3. After a few edits, `view` the file: the H1 / intro block has been re-injected multiple times, nested inside unrelated sections, and the file size has ballooned.

title: fix: tolerate unregistered LanguageModelIgnoredFileProvider handle in $isFileIgnored (fixes #323156)
body:
### Summary `ExtHostLanguageModels.$isFileIgnored` throws `Unknown LanguageModelIgnoredFileProvider` when it receives an RPC for a provider `handle` that is no longer in its local `_ignoredFileProviders` map. This is a benign cross-process **use-after-dispose / stale-handle race** across the main-thread → extension-host RPC boundary: the extHost deletes its local provider entry synchronously on disposal while the main-thread registration is briefly still live (the `$unregisterFileIgnoreProvider` RPC is async), or while an `$isFileIgnored` call is already in flight the other way. The throw surfaces as an unhandled error in extHost telemetry. The issue's stable-anomaly comment reports this as a **pre-existing bucket** that spiked **60.5×** at the `1.125.1 → 1.126.0` boundary (121 users / 230 hits), with the signal "a missing guard when the provider handle is gone" — i.e. the frequency rose but the underlying defect is old. The fix adds the missing guard: return `false` (not ignored) for an unknown handle instead of throwing, matching the default the main-thread `LanguageModelIgnoredFilesService.fileIsIgnored` already returns when no provider is registered. Fixes microsoft/vscode#323156 Recommended reviewer: `@roblourens` ### Culprit Commit The throw is **pre-existing**, introduced together with the feature in `bcf6a6af1c18a27b00069f7713d8bc063bcadc33` — "Add LanguageModelIgnoredFileProvider (#231696)" by `@roblourens` (2024-10-18). Confirmed against that PR's source: the original `$isFileIgnored` already did `if (!provider) { throw new Error('Unknown LanguageModelIgnoredFileProvider'); }`. Keep an editor active so `ChatImplicitContext` periodically calls `fileIsIgnored` on the active resource. 3. The chosen value is exactly the default the main-thread `LanguageModelIgnoredFilesService.fileIsIgnored` already returns when no provider is registered, so behavior is consistent on both sides of the boundary. title: fix: preserve ENOTEMPTY error code in extension rename (fixes #323155)
body:
### Summary

`extractUserExtension` installs an extension by extracting the VSIX into a temporary directory and then renaming that temp directory to the final extension location. When two sources install the same extension concurrently (for example a built-in language pack being auto-updated while it is also installed by another path), the final directory already exists and the rename fails with `ENOTEMPTY`. The call site explicitly treats this as a **benign race** and swallows it — but the check `error.code === 'ENOTEMPTY'` never matched, so the benign race was re-thrown as an unhandled error into telemetry:

`ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rename '.../extensions/.6de5c025-...' -> '.../extensions/ms-ceintl.vscode-language-pack-ja-1.126....'`

The root cause is that the private `rename()` helper wraps **every** failure with `toExtensionManagementError(error, ExtensionManagementErrorCode.Rename)`, which constructs a new `ExtensionManagementError` whose `.code` is set to the enum value `'Rename'`. This clobbers the original `'ENOTEMPTY'` code before the caller ever sees it, so the benign-race branch is effectively dead code.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#323155
Recommended reviewer: `@sandy081`

### Culprit Commit

The error-code-clobbering bug is **latent / pre-existing**: both the benign-race handler in `extractUserExtension` and the wrapping `rename()` helper already exist unchanged in `7f503b81` and earlier, so neither was introduced inside the observed telemetry window.

What turned this latent bug into a high-volume bucket is `143b631d` — "Enable auto-update for built-in extensions" (Sandeep Somavarapu / `@sandy081`, 2026-03-31), a confirmed ancestor of the shipped commit `7e7950df` (1.126.0). Enabling auto-update for built-in extensions routes bundled language packs such as `ms-ceintl.vscode-language-pack-ja` through the same extract→rename path, dramatically increasing the concurrent-install race that produces the benign `ENOTEMPTY`. The bucket first appears in `1.119.0` (the first stable release carrying this feature) and persists through `1.126.0`.

Later commits in the same feature line (`7f503b81`, `88e21a0` "handle edge cases while updating built in extensions") touched neighbouring update logic but did not repair the broken `ENOTEMPTY` detection.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[extractUserExtension extracts VSIX to temp dir] --> B[calls rename temp to final]
    B --> C[pfs.Promises.rename]
    C -- final dir already exists --> D[throws raw error with code ENOTEMPTY]
    D --> E{rename helper catch block}
    E -- before fix --> F[wraps via toExtensionManagementError with code Rename]
    F --> G{caller catch checks for ENOTEMPTY}
    G -- no the code is now Rename --> H[else branch re-throws]
    H --> I[unhandled error reaches telemetry]
    E -- after fix --> J[re-throws raw ENOTEMPTY]
    J --> K{caller catch checks for ENOTEMPTY}
    K -- yes --> L[logs info deletes temp swallows benign race]
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/node/extensionManagementService.ts` — the `ExtensionsScanner.rename()` helper (producer of the mis-coded error) and the `extractUserExtension()` benign-race handler that consumes `error.code`. **Modified.**

Supporting context (not modified):
- `src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/common/abstractExtensionManagementService.ts` — `toExtensionManagementError()` constructs the wrapped error that dropped the original `.code`.
- `src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/common/extensionManagement.ts` — `ExtensionManagementError` sets `.code`/`.name` to the enum value.
- `src/vs/base/node/pfs.ts` — `rename`/`renameWithRetry` retries only `EACCES`/`EPERM`/`EBUSY`, so `ENOTEMPTY` surfaces immediately with its raw code.

### Repro Steps

1. On a remote/server install, have a built-in language pack (for example `ms-ceintl.vscode-language-pack-ja`) eligible for auto-update.
2. Cause the extension to be installed/updated by two sources at once (auto-update of the built-in plus another install path), so the final extension directory is created by one path while the other is mid-extract.
3. The second path finishes extracting into its temp dir and calls `rename(temp → final)`; the final directory already exists, so `pfs.Promises.rename` throws `ENOTEMPTY`.
4. Before this fix, the helper rewraps the error as `Rename`, the caller's `error.code === 'ENOTEMPTY'` benign-race check fails, and the error is re-thrown into telemetry instead of being swallowed.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/node/extensionManagementService.ts`, `ExtensionsScanner.rename()`:

The mis-coded error object is produced inside `rename()` at the `toExtensionManagementError(error, ...Rename)` call — that is where a raw `ENOTEMPTY` is turned into an `ExtensionManagementError` whose `.code` becomes `'Rename'`. The fix adds a guard **at that producer**, before the wrapping throw: if the caught error's code is `ENOTEMPTY`, re-throw it unchanged; otherwise keep the existing `Rename` wrapping. This restores the original author's intent — the caller's benign-race branch (`error.code === 'ENOTEMPTY'`) becomes reachable again, so the concurrent-install race is logged and swallowed, while every genuine rename failure is still wrapped as `Rename` and its telemetry classification is preserved.

This follows the fix-at-the-data-producer principle rather than patching the crash site: the guard lives where the bad error object is created, not at the caller's `catch` where the symptom surfaces. No `try/catch` was added (the existing one is reused), no `logService` call was removed, and no genuine error is silenced — only the already-intended benign race is allowed to reach its existing handler.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Matching the wrapped error by message text at the caller's `catch` — rejected: a consumer-side string-match hack at the crash site that does not address where `.code` is lost.
- Making `toExtensionManagementError()` itself preserve `ENOTEMPTY` — rejected: it is a shared helper used by many unrelated callers, so special-casing one filesystem code there is too broad.

### Recommended Owner

`@sandy081` (Sandeep Somavarapu) — owns the extension management area, authored the built-in-extension auto-update feature that made this race hot, and is the author of essentially every recent change to `extensionManagementService.ts`.

title: chat/voice: land voice answers on question carousels (fix Skipped)
body:
## Summary

Lets voice users answer VS Code chat **question carousel** multi-question forms (and approvals) by voice. Fixes the end-to-end break where a voice-spoken selection never landed and the card showed "Skipped".

Three commits, stacked on `meganrogge/voice-mode-fixes`:

1. **`respond_to_session` answer/approval plumbing** — voice tool dispatch routes question-carousel answers and approvals back into the chat session.
2. **Complete agent-host carousels so voice answers land** — agent-host carousels resolve **only** via their completion promise (`carousel.dismiss(answers)` → `ChatInputCompleted`), not the event the voice path fired. The answer branch now calls `carousel.dismiss(toCarouselAnswers(answers))` in addition to `notifyQuestionCarouselAnswer`. An empty answer record maps to `undefined` so a genuine skip becomes Cancel rather than a truthy empty Accept. Adds a pure `toCarouselAnswers` helper + unit tests.
3. **Guard against stale skip overwrite** — after an external `dismiss()`, a later `onDidSubmitRequest` auto-skip could call `handleSubmit(defaults)` and overwrite the resolved answers. `skip()`/`ignore()` now also guard on `carousel.isUsed`. Adds 2 regression tests.

## Testing

- `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — 0 errors
- eslint on changed files — 0 errors
- Added unit + regression tests for `toCarouselAnswers` and the carousel skip/ignore guards.

title: Display model name in subagent session
body:
Fixes #321923

This pull request improves the Chat subagent UI by displaying the model name used by a subagent inline in the title and ensuring it is included in accessibility labels. It also adds tests to verify this behavior and introduces a dedicated CSS class for consistent styling of the model label.

### UI improvements
- The model name (e.g. "GPT-4o", "Claude Sonnet 4") is now shown inline in the subagent title if available, both while the tool is active and after completion. The label is updated in place to avoid duplication and is refreshed dynamically when the model arrives via metadata updates.

### Accessibility improvements
- The model name is now included in the `aria-label` for the collapse button so screen readers announce the model being used. Aria-label generation is centralized and updated whenever the title changes.

### Code structure
- `ChatCollapsibleContentPart.updateAriaLabel` is now `protected` to allow overriding, and is overridden in `ChatSubagentContentPart` to centralize aria-label generation.

### Testing
- Adds tests verifying the model name appears in the title and aria-label across states (active, completed, after metadata updates, after expand/collapse) and that no duplication occurs.

title: fix: handle failed terminal quick fix model request to avoid unhandled rejection (fixes #323149)
body:
### Summary The Copilot terminal quick fix command (`github.copilot.terminal.fixTerminalLastCommand`) reports an unhandled promise rejection to error telemetry — `Encountered an error while fetching quick fix file context: failed` — whenever the underlying chat/model request returns a non-success result. In `generateTerminalFixes` (`terminalFixGenerator.ts`), the result picks are produced with the explicit-promise anti-pattern `new Promise(r => generator.generateTerminalQuickFix(...).then(fixes => { ...; r(picks); }))`. The `.then()` has **no rejection handler**. `generateTerminalQuickFix` legitimately *throws* when a chat fetch returns a non-success type (network/model/rate-limit/filtered). With no rejection handler two things break at once: 1. The rejection is never handled → surfaced as an `unhandlederror` in error telemetry. 2. `r(picks)` is never called → the outer `picksPromise` never settles → `await picksPromise` hangs forever and the quick pick is stranded on "Generating...". The fix adds a rejection handler at the fire-and-forget boundary that logs the failure and resolves with an empty result, reusing the existing "No fixes found" UX. The intentional throw at the failure site is left untouched so the failure is still observable. Fixes microsoft/vscode#323149 Recommended reviewer: `@meganrogge` ### Culprit Commit Not a regression introduced by a single commit — this is a **pre-existing defect**. Evidence: - The error bucket has hits spread across **every** shipped extension version (0.46.2 → 0.53.1), with first-seen timestamps clustered inside a single ~6‐hour window on 2026‐06‐24, concentrated in 0.52.0 and 0.53.1. That signature is a transient backend/model failure spike that simultaneously exercised an always-present-but-rarely-hit failure path across all versions — not a code change landing in one version. - The most recent change to the file, `ef061ccb` (2026‐05‐14, `@vritant24`), only renamed the model id `copilot-fast` → `copilot-utility-small`; it did not introduce the throw or the missing rejection handler. - A precise `git blame` was not possible in this environment (shallow clone, `fetch-depth=1`), but the cross-version bucket history is sufficient to classify the missing-handler pattern as long-standing. So: the **trigger** was a transient spike of non-success chat fetch results on 2026‐06‐24; the **root-cause code defect** is the missing rejection handler that turns that expected failure into an unhandled rejection plus a stuck quick pick. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["User: run command that fails in terminal"] --> B["Command github.copilot.terminal.fixTerminalLastCommand
(conversationFeature.ts:279)"] B --> C["generateTerminalFixes(instantiationService)
terminalFixGenerator.ts:54"] C --> D["picksPromise = new Promise(r =>...)
:60"] D --> E[".generateTerminalQuickFix(...).then(fixes => ...)
:61 — NO rejection handler"] E --> F["generateTerminalQuickFix(...)
:136"] F --> G["_generateTerminalQuickFixFileContext(...)
:218"] G --> H["endpoint.makeChatRequest(...)
:229"] H --> I{"fetchResult.type === 'success'?"} I -- "no (e.g. 'failed')" --> J["throw new Error('Encountered an error
while fetching quick fix file context: failed')
:240-241"] J --> K["rejection propagates up through
generateTerminalQuickFix (await at :137)"] K --> L["reaches .then() with no onRejected
:61"] L --> M["UNHANDLED REJECTION → error telemetry"] L --> N["r(picks) never called → picksPromise never settles"] N --> O["await picksPromise hangs :108 → quick pick stuck on 'Generating...'"] ``` ### Affected Files - `extensions/copilot/src/extension/conversation/vscode-node/terminalFixGenerator.ts` — `generateTerminalFixes` (the fire-and-forget caller). The fix adds a rejection handler to the `.then()` at lines 61–89. The throw sites at `:184-186` and `:240-242` (inside `TerminalQuickFixGenerator`) are intentional failure signaling and are **not** modified. ### Repro Steps 1. Run a command in the integrated terminal that fails (so a terminal command-match result is available). 2. Invoke the Copilot terminal quick fix command `github.copilot.terminal.fixTerminalLastCommand`. 3. Force the model/chat request to return a non-success result (e.g. simulate a network/model failure or trigger it during a backend outage such as the 2026‐06‐24 spike), so `makeChatRequest` yields `fetchResult.type !== 'success'`. 4. Observe: an unhandled promise rejection (`Encountered an error while fetching quick fix file context: failed`) is reported to error telemetry, and the quick pick stays stuck showing "Generating..." indefinitely. With the fix: the failure is logged via `ILogService.error`, the quick pick resolves to the existing "No fixes found" state, and no unhandled rejection is reported. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `extensions/copilot/src/extension/conversation/vscode-node/terminalFixGenerator.ts`, `generateTerminalFixes`: Add an `onRejected` handler as the second argument to the existing `.then(fixes => { ... })` (bypass/defect site: the handler-less `.then()` at `terminalFixGenerator.ts:61`): ```ts }, err => { // Generating terminal fixes is best-effort: a failed model request rejects here. // Surface it as "No fixes found" instead of leaving an unhandled rejection that // also strands the quick pick on "Generating...". instantiationService.invokeFunction(accessor => accessor.get(ILogService)).error(err); r([]); }); ``` Why this is the correct fix: - It fixes the defect at the fire-and-forget boundary where the rejection actually escapes (the handler-less `.then()`), not at the crash site. The throw inside `_generateTerminalQuickFixFileContext` is deliberate failure signaling for an expected runtime condition; suppressing it there would hide a real failure from the rest of the method and from telemetry. The right place to decide "what the user sees when fix generation fails" is the command handler. - It is not error-masking: the failure is still recorded via `ILogService.error(err)` (no `logService.error` call is removed, no `try/catch` is added around the throwing code). title: fix: drop diagnostics with missing range at the language diagnostics boundary (fixes #323148)
body:
### Summary The bundled `GitHub.copilot-chat` extension throws an unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'start')` from `src/extension/xtab/common/lintErrors.ts:44`. The crash happens when copilot's Next-Edit (xtab) telemetry path reads diagnostics produced by *other* extensions: a third-party extension can publish a `vscode.Diagnostic` whose `range` is `undefined` (violating the non-nullable `range: Range` type via an `any`/plain-JS bypass). VS Code core returns that object verbatim through `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics()`, and copilot dereferences `diagnostic.range.start` without validating it. This is a recent regression: the error bucket first appears in extension version `0.53.0` and spikes in `0.53.1`, coinciding with the introduction of the `LintErrors.getData()` telemetry path that scans **every** file's diagnostics from **every** extension (via `getAllDiagnostics()`), dramatically widening exposure to malformed diagnostics from unrelated extensions. The fix sanitizes diagnostics at copilot's extension-host boundary (`LanguageDiagnosticsServiceImpl`), dropping entries with a missing `range` and logging the occurrence, so every consumer is protected once. Fixes microsoft/vscode#323148 Recommended reviewer: `@not-determined` ### Culprit Commit Not precisely identified. The repository is a shallow clone (`fetch-depth=1`) and history commands are unavailable in this environment, so `git blame`/`git log` could not pinpoint the introducing commit. Bucket history places the regression window at extension version `0.53.0` (where the bucket first appears) through `0.53.1` (where it spikes). The shipped-commit upper bound recorded on the issue is `7e7950df89d055b5a378379db9ee14290772148a`. The regression aligns with the addition of the `LintErrors.getData()` telemetry path (`xtabProvider.ts` → `_diagnostics(undefined)` → `getAllDiagnostics()`), which began scanning all extensions' diagnostics rather than only the active document's. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Third-party extension publishes vscode.Diagnostic with range = undefined
bypasses non-nullable range: Range via an any-cast] --> B[VS Code core ExtHostDiagnostics.getDiagnostics
returns the original objects verbatim, no range re-validation] B --> C[copilot LanguageDiagnosticsServiceImpl.getAllDiagnostics
returned the API result verbatim — BOUNDARY / fix site] C --> D[LintErrors.getData → _diagnostics undefined
xtabProvider.ts:427 fire-and-forget telemetry] D --> E[lintErrors.ts:44 new Range diagnostic.range.start.line + 1, ...
CRASH: Cannot read properties of undefined reading start] ``` ### Affected Files - `extensions/copilot/src/platform/languages/vscode/languageDiagnosticsServiceImpl.ts` — **(fixed)** copilot's extension-host boundary wrapping `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics()`. Now drops diagnostics with a missing `range` and logs the occurrence. - `extensions/copilot/src/extension/xtab/common/lintErrors.ts` — crash site (`line 44`, inside `_diagnostics`) and the `getData()` telemetry path that triggered the regression. Unchanged; protected by the boundary fix. - `extensions/copilot/src/platform/languages/common/languageDiagnosticsService.ts` — declares the `ILanguageDiagnosticsService` contract and the `rangeSpanningDiagnostics` / `getDiagnosticsAtSelection` utilities that also dereference `.range`. Unchanged; protected. - Other consumers of the same diagnostics that dereference `.range` and are likewise protected by the single boundary fix: `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/getErrorsTool.tsx`, `extensions/copilot/src/platform/tasks/vscode/tasksService.ts`. ### Repro Steps 1. Install/run alongside any extension that publishes a `vscode.Diagnostic` with an `undefined` `range` (e.g. constructing the object via `as any` / plain JS rather than the `vscode.Diagnostic` constructor) for some open file. 2. With `GitHub.copilot-chat` `0.53.x` active, trigger the Next-Edit (xtab) flow so `LintErrors.getData()` runs and calls `_diagnostics(undefined)` → `getAllDiagnostics()`. 3. As the malformed diagnostic is scanned, `lintErrors.ts:44` dereferences `diagnostic.range.start` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'start')` is thrown and reported to error telemetry. Note: exact end-user reproduction depends on a third-party extension emitting a contract-violating diagnostic; the boundary is reached on the non-blocking telemetry path regardless of which extension is responsible. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `extensions/copilot/src/platform/languages/vscode/languageDiagnosticsServiceImpl.ts`: `getDiagnostics(resource)` and `getAllDiagnostics()` now route their results through a new private `_dropMalformedDiagnostics(...)` helper that filters out any diagnostic whose `range` is `null`/`undefined` before returning. When entries are dropped, it emits a one-line `ILogService.warn` (the service now injects `@ILogService` via DI) recording how many were ignored. This fixes the bug at the data producer / trust boundary rather than at the crash site. `LanguageDiagnosticsServiceImpl` is the single seam where untrusted diagnostics from *all* extensions enter copilot, and at least six call sites dereference `diagnostic.range` downstream (`lintErrors.ts:44`, `getErrorsTool.tsx`, `tasksService.ts`, plus the `rangeSpanningDiagnostics` and `getDiagnosticsAtSelection` utilities). When the same typed property must be guarded at multiple independent callers, that is the signal to fix the producer once — so validating at the boundary protects every consumer with a single change. Because `vscode.Diagnostic.range` is declared non-nullable, a missing range is a genuine contract violation from outside copilot's control; dropping the entry at the boundary is the standard way to validate untrusted extension-host input, and the paired `warn` keeps the violation observable instead of silently swallowing it. After this change, `LanguageDiagnosticsServiceImpl.getAllDiagnostics`/`getDiagnostics` cannot return a `vscode.Diagnostic` whose `range` is null/undefined, because `_dropMalformedDiagnostics` removes every such entry before returning, so no downstream consumer can dereference an undefined `range`. **Alternatives considered:** - Guard the crash site in `lintErrors.ts:44` (skip diagnostics with no range there): rejected because it only protects one of several consumers and sits at the symptom, leaving the other `.range` dereferences (`getErrorsTool.tsx`, `tasksService.ts`, the diagnostics utilities) still exposed to the same malformed input. - Wrap the dereference in `try/catch`: rejected because it would hide the contract violation from telemetry without fixing the source of the bad data. ### Recommended Owner `@not-determined`. title: NES: cache cross-file suggestions under the active document
body:
## What

Extends Next Edit Suggestion (NES) caching to support **cross-file** suggestions — a suggestion the model returns for a document _other_ than the one being edited.

Previously a cross-file suggestion was cached only under the **target** document's content (`B(content) → edit`), so it could only be re-served from cache after the user navigated to B. This change **additionally** caches it under the **active** document:

```
A(content + edit window) → edit-in-B
```

so the cross-file suggestion can be re-served from cache while the cursor is still in A — the same place it was produced.

## How

- **Cache (`nextEditCache.ts`)** — `CachedEdit`/`CachedEditOpts` gain `targetDocId?` (the document the edit applies to, when different from the key document) and `targetDocumentBeforeEdit?` (a snapshot of that document's content the edit's offsets index into). The cursor-distance rejection is skipped for cross-file entries (their edit is in the target's coordinate space), while edit-window gating — which is in the active document's coordinates — is kept.

- **Provider write path (`nextEditProvider.ts`)** — when the first streamed edit targets a different document, a small helper also stores the A‑keyed cross-file entry (exact content match only, never rebased). At stream end the active document is **no longer** cached as "no edit" when a cross-file entry was just stored under the same key, which would otherwise clobber it. Applied to both the normal and speculative paths.

- **Provider read path (`nextEditProvider.ts`)** — a cross-file cache hit is served only while its target document is **open** and **byte-identical** to the stored snapshot. Otherwise the hit is treated as a **cache miss → fresh fetch**, rather than serving a misplaced edit or getting stuck re-serving a dead entry until the active document changes.

This is always on (no config flag).

## Two invalidation layers

1. **Default config** — editing the target document already purges cross-document cache entries (the existing `InlineEditsTriggerOnEditorChangeAfterSeconds` purge, default `10`).
2. **Read-path validity guard** — additionally covers the closed-target case (closing isn't an edit, so no purge) and the purge-disabled configuration.

## Tests

7 cross-file tests in `nextEditProviderCaching.spec.ts`, assertions are behavioral (served edit + provider call-count, deterministically waiting for the first request's stream-end before re-requesting):

- re-serves on a 2nd trigger in A and survives the no-suggestions stream-end (no clobber);
- re-serves within / refetches outside the cached edit window;
- refetches when the target document is closed;
- control: with the purge disabled and the target unchanged, re-serves from cache (isolates the guard);
- refetches when the target changed — once with the purge disabled (guard fires) and once under the default config (purge fires).

## Validation

- `nextEditProviderCaching.spec.ts`: 11/11 pass; broader NES suite: 89 pass / 2 pre-existing skips.
- Typecheck (`tsgo --noEmit`) and eslint clean on all changed files.

## Out of scope

- Rebasing the active-document-keyed entry across edits in the active document (exact-match only).
- Hardening the _fresh_ cross-file path against the target changing in-flight (pre-existing; subsequent re-serves are already protected by the new guard).

- `changesViewService.ts:86` — `folders[0].gitRepository` → `folders[0]?.gitRepository`
- `copilotChatSessionsChangesets.ts` (lines 30, 60, 190, 242) — same null-safe access

title: Sessions: folders[0].gitRepository access throws TypeError when a session workspace has no folders

Several places in the Sessions feature access `workspace.folders[0].gitRepository` without optional chaining. The workspace type is `readonly folders: ISessionFolder[]` with no non-empty guarantee, so when a session has a workspace but an empty `folders` array, `folders[0]` is `undefined` and `.gitRepository` throws a `TypeError`. Elsewhere in `src/vs/sessions/` the convention is null-safe access (`folders[0]?.`), even guarded explicitly with `workspace.folders.length > 0` in `sessionsActions.ts`. These 5 spots diverge from that convention.

### Fix

I have already made the change locally (adding optional chaining to match the existing convention) and it is ready to submit as a PR.

title: sessions: header changes pill opens the default changeset
body:
## What

The Agents window session **header diff-stats pill** now opens the **default changeset** when activated, matching the stats it displays.

## Why

The pill's label reflects the session's **default** changeset (`isDefault`). But activating the pill opens the shared per-session multi-diff editor, whose file list comes from the Changes view's `activeSessionChangesObs` — which is **selected-or-default**. So after the user manually picks a different changeset in the Changes view (e.g. Uncommitted Changes, Last Turn), the pill's label (default changeset stats) and the diff it opened (selected changeset) could disagree.

## How

Reset the Changes view changeset selection to the default (`setChangesetId(undefined)`) before opening the diff editor. This keeps the pill, the diff editor, and the Changes view panel all aligned on the default changeset.

## Notes for reviewers

- Follow-up to #323101, which fixed the pill's displayed stats to read the default changeset; this aligns what the pill *opens* with what it *shows*.
- The Changes view already resets the selection to the default on every active-session change, so this only affects the case where the user changed the selection within the current session and then clicks the header pill.

## Testing

- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅ (compiles all layers)
- Problems/type check on the changed file ✅
- Manual: select a non-default changeset in the Changes view, then click the header pill — the opened diff now matches the pill's stats (the default changeset).

title: sessions: pre-select archived session's folder on return to new-session view
body:
## Problem

When marking a session as done (archiving) and being sent back to the New Session view, the workspace picker showed the **last user-picked folder** (from storage) instead of the **folder of the session that was just archived**.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create session in folder A
2. Create session in folder B  
3. Reopen session A and mark it as done
4. **Expected:** New Session view pre-selects folder A
5. **Actual:** New Session view selects folder B

## Root Cause

In `_activeSessionViewListeners`, when the active session becomes archived, `openNewSession()` was called with no arguments. This causes a fresh `NewChatWidget` (and `WorkspacePicker`) to be created, which restores its selection from profile storage — which holds folder B (the last user-picked folder), not the folder of the session being closed.

## Fix

Pass the archived session's workspace folder URI to `openNewSession`. When `openNewSession` receives a `folderUri`, it creates a draft session for that folder and activates it. The new `NewChatWidget`'s `render()` then calls `_syncWorkspacePickerFromActiveSession()`, which finds the draft for folder A and silently syncs the workspace picker to it — keeping the user in the right context.

Falls back to the existing no-folder path when the session has no workspace.

- **Linux & macOS:** prompt `run in shell: cat ~/something.txt`
  - With **default approvals**: the sandbox blocks the read and the model offers to **run outside the sandbox** ("Run in terminal outside the sandbox?").

"github.copilot.chat.cli.sandbox.enabled": "allowNetwork"
```

| **Severity** | 🔴 High — Console flooding, performance degradation, potential extension loading failures |

## Possible Trigger Conditions

1. **Missing Extension Dependencies**: An extension's required module is not installed or path is misconfigured
2. **Resource URI Resolution Failure**: `$loadForeignModule` cannot correctly resolve the extension's resource path
3. **Cache Corruption**: Extension compilation cache or path mapping cache is corrupted
4. **Extension Conflicts**: Race condition when multiple extensions load simultaneously

## Suggested Fix Directions

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Discover toUrl undefined error] --> B{Check call stack}
    B --> C[$loadForeignModule params valid?]
    C -->|No| D[Check extension manifest config]
    C -->|Yes| E[asBrowserUri return value correct?]
    E -->|No| F[Check resource path mapping]
    E -->|Yes| G[toUri object is undefined?]
    G -->|Yes| H[Add undefined check / null guard]
    H --> I[Add Promise catch to prevent retry loop]

```

- **VSCode Version**: Latest stable
- **OS**: macOS Darwin 24.6.0
- **Reproduction Timing**: Triggered during file edit/modify operations
- **Trigger Extension**: To be further identified (likely related to file watching/module loading)

| User Experience | 🔴 Severe — Console flooding impairs debugging |
| Performance | 🟡 Medium — Excessive error logs consume CPU/memory |
| Stability | 🟡 Medium — May cause extension loading failures |
| Data Security | 🟢 None — No data leakage involved |

## Additional Notes

This error log is triggered when the user performs file editing operations. The error repeats at an extremely high frequency in the console, forming a **Log Storm** caused by unhandled Promise rejections leading to an infinite retry loop.

---

## Summary for Issue Submission

**Title**: Console spam: `toUrl` undefined error — Unhandled Promise rejection causes infinite retry loop

**Key Problem**:
- `nP.toUri()` accesses `undefined.toUrl()` triggering `TypeError`
- `$loadForeignModule` contains unhandled Promise (no `catch`), error is re-thrown

1. Add null/undefined guard in `toUri`/`asBrowserUri`

title: sessions: always show New Chat action in session header
body:
## What

In the Agents window session header, the **New Chat** action is now rendered as a labeled `+ New Chat` button and is always available, sitting next to the **Conversations** menu and the session controls.

| State | Header |
| --- | --- |
| Single open chat | `[+ New Chat]  [Conversations*]  |  ✓ 📌 ✕` |
| Tab strip shown (more than one open chat) | header New Chat hidden; the tab strip offers its own `+` |

\* Conversations still only appears once the session has more than one committed chat.

## Changes

- **New Chat rendering** is contributed by the action itself: `SessionNewChatActionViewItemContribution` registers a `SessionHeaderMetaActionViewItem` for the New Chat command via `IActionViewItemService`. The header toolbar stays generic — it no longer special-cases the action by id.
- **Always shown**: New Chat moved into `SessionBarToolbar` (navigation group, order 0). It is hidden only when the chat tab strip is shown, gated by a new `SessionHasMultipleOpenChats` context key (`openChats > 1`); the tab strip then offers New Chat at the end of the tabs.
- **Conversations**: unchanged behaviour from `main` (header only, once there is more than one committed chat).
- **Mark as Done** moved into the `1_session` group so it groups with Pin / Close (removes the stray separator before them).
- **Spacing**: header toolbar action items now have a small gap so New Chat and Conversations no longer render flush.
- Updated the accessibility help text accordingly.

## Notes for reviewers

- The one-shot `onDidRegister` event fired after `register()` is intentional: it makes header toolbars that were already built (e.g. for a session restored before the `AfterRestored` contribution runs) re-render and pick up the labeled rendering. Same idiom as `NewSessionActionViewItemContribution` / `ViewAllChangesActionViewItemContribution`.

title: sessions: add quick-navigate support to the sessions picker
body:
## Summary

Pressing the sessions picker keybinding (`Ctrl+R` / `Ctrl+R` on Mac) while holding the modifier now cycles through the session list instead of reopening the picker — mirroring the `Ctrl+Tab` editor-switcher UX:

1. Hold modifier → press trigger: picker opens with the active session focused
2. Keep holding → press trigger again: next session focused (`Shift` reverses direction)
3. Release modifier: focused session is opened

## Implementation

The implementation reuses the same three-part recipe as the workbench editor switcher (`Ctrl+Tab`):

1. **`picker.quickNavigate`** is set from the command's own keybindings. The platform's built-in `KEY_UP` listener in `QuickPick` then accepts the focused item when the modifier is released — no custom code needed for that half.

2. **`SessionsPickerVisibleContext`** — a new context key, set while the picker is open and reset on hide. This scopes the navigate keybindings so they only fire when the picker is actually showing.

3. **Two `KeybindingsRegistry` rules** (`navigateNext` / `navigatePrevious`) bound to the same chord at `SessionsContrib + 50` weight call `getQuickNavigateHandler`, which forwards to `quickInputService.navigate()`. The higher weight ensures these win over the show-command when the picker is already open.

## Files changed

- `src/vs/sessions/common/contextkeys.ts` — adds `SessionsPickerVisibleContext`
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsActions.ts` — wires up `quickNavigate`, context key lifecycle, and navigate keybinding rules
